name: Zhen Li
title: Ph.D. Candidate in Mathematics
summary: I am a Ph.D. candidate at the School of Mathematics, Southwest Jiaotong University. My research focuses on coding theory for synchronization errors, including insertion/deletion channels, localized and burst edit errors, segmented channels, and DNA data storage. I am particularly interested in low-redundancy constructions with transparent combinatorial structure and efficient encoding/decoding algorithms.

researchInterests.title: Synchronization-error correcting codes
researchInterests.description: Low-redundancy codes for insertions, deletions, burst errors, localized edits, and substring edits, with attention to both existential bounds and efficient constructions.

researchInterests.title: DNA data storage and synthesis coding
researchInterests.description: Coding methods for parallel DNA synthesis, synthesis repeats/defects, constrained synthesis, and robust storage under structured biochemical error models.

researchInterests.title: Segmented and marker-based channel coding
researchInterests.description: Marker+codeword+marker structures, VT-style constraints, and linear-time encoders/decoders for segmented single-insdel and single-edit channels.

researchInterests.title: Finite-field methods and sequence design
researchInterests.description: Earlier work on power functions, Walsh transforms, differential spectra, boomerang uniformity, complementary sequences, and related cyclic codes.

projects.title: Coding for DNA Synthesis Repeats
projects.description: Developing codes for synchronized repeat errors in massively parallel DNA synthesis, including known-repeat and unknown-repeat decoding regimes.

projects.title: Segmented Edit-Error Correcting Codes
projects.description: Designing marker-based constructions for segmented single-insdel and single-edit channels with low redundancy and linear-time encoding/decoding.

projects.title: Localized Edit Codes via Local Confusability
projects.description: Studying local confusability graph methods and window-lifting techniques for burst deletions, localized deletions, and bounded substring edits.
